The Museum of Moroccan Jewish Culture opened in the city of Fez and makes history as the first museum dedicated to Jewish culture paid for by public funds of an Arab Muslim country. The museum explores 2,500 years of rich Jewish history in the country including archaeological artifacts, art, manuscripts, and other traditions passed down from generation to generation. You are greeted by a sign at the front of the building inscribed in four languages including Arabic, Amazigh, Hebrew, and French. It’s so inspiring to see Jewish culture preserved and given space to be taught to new visitors 💙 🎥: M24 TV
